The entry checks all three denominator limbs before the numerator. A zero denominator returns status 2 even for 0/0; a zero numerator with nonzero denominator returns a zero Decimal. records.body:
## Summary

An 88-byte single-call window at `0x5650a60` (node #94) that derives a
nonzero flag from its 32-bit second argument with a bit trick, then
applies one shared callee to two fields of its object: it calls
`0x5656fc0` with `(obj+0x60, obj+0x60, flag, 0x918940)` and tail-jumps
to the same callee with `(obj+0x90, obj+0x90, flag, 0x918940)`. One flag
derivation, one call, one tail jump: no branch, no loop, no second
distinct callee. The callee's behavior is excluded from the rule; only
its identity and extent are locked.

## Rule

Let `n = movsxd(esi)` (the 32-bit second argument, sign-extended to 64
bits) and `flag = (n != 0) ? 1 : 0`. Then:

1. Call `0x5656fc0` with `rdi = obj+0x60`, `rsi = obj+0x60`,
   `rdx = flag`, `rcx = 0x918940`.
2. Tail-jump to `0x5656fc0` with `rdi = obj+0x90`, `rsi = obj+0x90`,
   `rdx = flag`, `rcx = 0x918940`.

The flag is derived before the calls and feeds both of them. That
ordering is disclosed, not hidden: the derivation is a genuine
computation (a new boolean from the input), not argument shuffling —
every shuffle-only candidate found in this hunt was rejected below.

## Window

- Start `0x5650a60`, end (exclusive) `0x5650ab8`, 88 bytes
- FDE section offset `0x002daa20`, CIE `0x00000000`
- Padding: 8 bytes int3 to the next FDE at `0x5650ac0`
- Body SHA-256
  `1145fa7fac82339f9c35b0c7884497a01fbdb551e9d2cbeda2e766e062190c66`
- Instruction walk: `endbr64; movsxd rsi, esi; push r12; mov rdx, rsi;
  sub rsi, 1; push rbp; mov rbp, rdi; not rdx; push rbx; and rdx, rsi;
  shr rdx, 63; lea r12, [rip-0x4d38146] (# 0x918940); mov rbx, rdx;
  lea rdi, [rdi+0x60]; xor rbx, 1; mov rsi, rdi; mov rcx, r12;
  mov rdx, rbx; call 0x5656fc0; lea rdi, [rbp+0x90]; mov rcx, r12;
  mov rdx, rbx; mov rsi, rdi; pop rbx; pop rbp; pop r12; jmp 0x5656fc0`
- The window has no `ret`: control leaves by tail jump to the callee.
- The bit trick: `flag = 1 ^ (((~n) & (n-1)) >> 63)`. Bit 63 of `~n` is
  1 exactly when `n >= 0`; bit 63 of `n-1` is 1 exactly when `n <= 0`
  (n is 32-bit sign-extended, so `n-1` cannot overflow the sign bit);
  their AND has bit 63 set exactly when `n == 0`. Shifting right by 63
  yields 1 exactly for `n == 0`, and `xor 1` flips it to the nonzero
  flag. No comparison instruction is involved.
- Rule edges: esi `0x00000000` -> flag 0; `0x00000001` -> 1;
  `0xffffffff` (n = -1) -> 1; `0x7fffffff` -> 1; `0x80000000`
  (n = -2147483648) -> 1. Edges are model checks on the recorded
  arithmetic, not executions of the target binary.

## Callee

- `0x5656fc0`, 217 bytes, FDE start, offset `0x002db3d4`, CIE
  `0x00000000`, 7 bytes NOP padding (`90 66 0f 1f 44 00 00`, not int3)
  to the next FDE at `0x56570a0`, body SHA-256
  `a160770fd4eb9469f74171b2863edc15b6e3e73373e354602155535cd006d2ca`
- Called from 47 direct sites in `.text`, including this window
  (`0x5650a9a`); the full list is recorded in `evidence.json` and
  re-derived by the checker. The other 46 sites sit inside larger
  functions, and no other small single-call window calls this callee, so
  the shared callee is not a shared rule — but the sharing is disclosed,
  not hidden.
- Because the callee is 217 bytes, its body is locked by length,
  SHA-256 and padding rather than per instruction; that locks its
  identity and extent, which is all the rule uses.

## Incoming calls

finds exactly one site, at `0x5640d6d` inside the 453-byte function

RE-001: bind node #94 object teardown 0x514bfe0 with its two string disposals

Task ID: RE-001. Bounded question: what does the 97-byte function at
0x514bfe0 in node #94 do to its input object — which fields does it
free, in what order, and how does it free the object itself?

Answer: it is a null-safe teardown. A null input returns at once with
no delete call. A non-null input has two embedded SSO strings disposed
(the +0x1a8 string first, then the +0x48 string), each freed only when
its pointer differs from its own inline-buffer address, with delete
size = union field + 1 (mod 2^64); the object itself is then deleted
with size 0x2e0 (736) via a tail jump to the _ZdlPvm PLT stub, so the
non-null path never returns to its caller.

Evidence (research/work-items/RE-001-object-teardown-94/, new format):
semantic records only in records.json — no per-instruction mnemonic

records.body:
## Summary

A 30-byte single-call window at `0x327b210` (node #94) that calls
`0x3597020` with pass-through arguments, then increments a field of the
returned object — unless the field holds the `-1` sentinel, in which
case it stays `-1` — and returns with `rax` restored. One call, one
load, one increment, one conditional move, one store: no branch, no
loop, no flag test other than the `inc` itself, no constant pool, no
second call. The callee's behavior is excluded from the rule; only its
identity and extent are locked.

## Rule

Call `0x3597020` with the window's incoming arguments unchanged, then
store `(old == -1 ? -1 : old + 1, wrapping)` as a qword to `[obj+0x20]`,
where `obj` is the callee's return value in `rax` and `old` is the
previous value of that field. Then `ret`, with `rax` restored to its
incoming value by the closing `pop rax`.

## Window

- Start `0x327b210`, end (exclusive) `0x327b22e`, 30 bytes
- FDE section offset `0x00104048`, CIE `0x00000000`
- Padding: 2 bytes int3 to the next FDE at `0x327b230`
- Body SHA-256
  `b58ca0301ff4ef99320862e6ba60ea112732924de3d9e05574c28f6096d7515b`
- Instruction walk: `push rax; call 0x3597020; mov rcx, [rax+0x20];
  inc rcx; mov rdx, -1; cmovne rdx, rcx; mov [rax+0x20], rdx;
  pop rax; ret`
- The window starts with `push rax`, not `endbr64`; its FDE range is
  still `0x327b210..0x327b22e`. The window's return value is the
  incoming `rax`, not the callee's return: the stored field is the
  window's only observable effect in this packet.
- The stickiness comes from the `inc` itself: `inc rcx` sets ZF exactly
  when the incremented value is zero, which happens exactly when the old
  value was `-1`, and `cmovne` keeps the `-1` in that case. No separate
  comparison instruction exists in the window.

## Callee

- `0x3597020`, 370 bytes, FDE start, offset `0x00151884`, CIE
  `0x00000000`, 14 bytes int3 padding, body SHA-256
  `62a7dcf9363b2b6e8be596ba401687524272180271d5a29573763c76ccb6f7ec`
- Called from exactly one direct site in `.text`: this window
  (`0x327b211`). No other small-band window shares this callee, so the
  shared-callee question does not arise.
- Because the callee is 370 bytes, its body is locked by length, SHA-256
  and padding rather than per instruction; that locks its identity and
  extent, which is all the rule uses.

## Incoming calls

A byte-pattern scan of `.text` for direct `e8` calls to `0x327b210`
finds exactly zero sites, so this packet has seven files (no caller
file). Register-indirect references, other pointer paths, prefixes, and
data sections are not a complete xref census.

## Twins and uniqueness

Raw FDE bytes, position-wise equal bytes, no normalization. Two claimed
cohorts: A = claimed windows present in the 20–150B single-call census
(30 windows, including #152); B = every claimed window from every
`evidence.json` in prior worktrees and the main tree (32 windows).

- Against claimed windows: maximum similarity 0.133 max-length
  (cohort A: at `0x4f9ee90`, the #147 window; cohort B: same window),
  well below the 0.60 cutoff.
- Against the full corpus of 31,898 single-call FDE windows: best
  non-self 0.167 max-length (at `0x538fb30`, 29 bytes: a call + lea/add
  + store window with a different rule) and 0.200 min-length with the
  20-byte floor (at `0x134cc70`, 72 bytes: a larger window sharing only
  short prologue bytes).
- The mnemonic skeleton is a singleton among 31,898 single-call FDE
  windows of 20-150 bytes, and this window is the only single-call
  census window calling `0x3597020`.
- Measure validation: the same procedure reproduces #152's
  claimed-best 0.250 max-length (cohort A at `0x54d6360`, cohort B at
  `0x55243d0`) and corpus-best 0.438 / 0.500 exactly, and #151's
  claimed-best 0.211 max / 0.235 min and corpus-best 0.333 / 0.439
  exactly.

## Rule edges

- old `0x0` -> `0x1` (ordinary increment)
- old `0x5` -> `0x6` (ordinary increment)
- old `0xffffffffffffffff` (-1) -> `0xffffffffffffffff` (sentinel
  sticks: `inc` yields 0, ZF set, `cmovne` keeps `-1`)
- old `0xfffffffffffffffe` (-2) -> `0xffffffffffffffff` (increments
  into the sentinel, then sticks on later calls)
- old `0x7fffffffffffffff` -> `0x8000000000000000` (wraps past the
  signed maximum; recorded as an edge, not a fault)

Edges are model checks on the recorded arithmetic, not executions of the
target binary. The increment wraps modulo 2^64; only the `-1` value is
sticky.

## Limits

- The callee's behavior is excluded; only its identity and extent are
  locked.
- The window's return value is the incoming `rax` (restored by
  `pop rax`); the stored field is its only observable effect.
- The gate depends on `inc` setting ZF: there is no separate comparison
  instruction, and no other instruction between `inc` and `cmovne`
  touches the flags (`mov` does not affect flags).
- Nearest-symbol annotations carry large offsets and are not
  identifications; no symbol name is claimed.
- The zero-caller claim covers direct `e8` calls in `.text` only.

Two quantity conversions use similar floating-point guards but have different factor and sign semantics. Treating them as one generic saturating unsigned conversion would change negative results and the handling of complementary factors.

## Evidence

For node #94 SHA-256 `3b7179cd967d1b13b683e05debfc685ad4c750e918226402d5d575eff1c0459f`, FDE ranges `[0x3c06160, 0x3c0620a)` and `[0x4cda1a0, 0x4cda253)` are in ELF virtual-address coordinates; the packet records their file offsets and full bytes. Both reject input words with the high bit set, test the product for non-finite values and use a truncating signed conversion. The first applies a nonnegative output clamp. The second subtracts the input factor from 1.0 and preserves a negative converted result. Both failure paths reference quantity source location line 843. Four binary64 constants and their file offsets are recorded from the ELF.

## Inferences

The closed-form Python model is a static interpretation under round-to-nearest binary64 arithmetic. It predicts that input 3 and factor 1.5 produce 4 and -1 respectively. The semantic names, the values' units, the caller contracts and the node's actual floating-point environment are unresolved.

## Reproduce

records.body:
## Summary

A 48-byte single-call window at `0x5335bf0` (node #94) that calls
`sysconf` (via the PLT stub at `0x5660210`) with `edi = 30`, applies a
threshold gate to the signed return value, stores the result to a `.bss`
global, and returns. One call, one compare, one conditional move, one
store: no branch, no loop, no second call, no constant pool. The
callee's behavior is excluded from the rule; only its identity is
locked.

## Rule

Call `sysconf` (PLT stub `0x5660210`) with `edi = 30` (other argument
registers pass through), then store `(signed ret <= 0x3ff ? 0x1000 :
ret)` as a qword to `.bss` address `0x578f8a0`, then `ret`.

## Window

- Start `0x5335bf0`, end (exclusive) `0x5335c20`, 48 bytes
- FDE section offset `0x002afe8c`, CIE `0x00000000`
- Padding: 0 bytes (the next FDE starts immediately at `0x5335c20`)
- Body SHA-256
  `76f470b82e265dfcc45e997f5c26b4af1b3efdf303b4e479bb2bed32d2656e2d`
- Instruction walk: `endbr64; sub rsp, 8; mov edi, 0x1e;
  call 0x5660210; mov edx, 0x1000; cmp rax, 0x3ff; cmovle rax, rdx;
  lea rdx, [rip+0x459c88]; mov [rdx], rax; add rsp, 8; ret`
- The window ends with a `ret`, not a tail jump. The comparison is
  signed: a negative return value floors to 4096, exactly like 0.

## Callee

The call target is not an FDE function: it is the 16-byte PLT stub for
the `sysconf` import.

- `0x5660210`, in `.plt`, stub bytes
  `ff251a8c11006812000000e9c0feffff`, stub SHA-256
  `04eb853e43cc64be6cfc060a3ff445c55c41c26b108d34540b66f632f6e34ffd`
- GOT slot `0x5778e30` (in `.got.plt`, value `0x5660216`, i.e. lazy
  binding unresolved)
- Relocation: `.rela.plt` entry, `r_offset = 0x5778e30`, type 7
  (`R_X86_64_JUMP_SLOT`), symbol `sysconf`
- FDE: none (no FDE covers `0x5660210`; the last FDE before it ends at
  `0x56600b0`)
- The import name comes from the binary's own relocation record, not
  from a nearest-symbol annotation; GNU objdump independently renders
  the call target as `<sysconf@plt>`.
- Called from 4 direct sites in `.text`: this window (`0x5335bfd`)
  and three sites inside two larger functions (`0x54ba193` and
  `0x54ba1a0` inside `0x54b9f30..0x54ba755`, 2085 bytes; `0x552d6e5`
  inside `0x552d6c0..0x552db37`, 1143 bytes). Only this window is a
  small single-call window, so the shared import is not a shared rule.
- Because the callee is a PLT stub, its body is locked by stub bytes,
  SHA-256, GOT slot, and relocation record rather than per
  instruction; that locks its identity, which is all the rule uses.

## Incoming calls

A byte-pattern scan of `.text` for direct `e8` calls to `0x5335bf0`
finds exactly zero sites, so this packet has seven files (no caller
file). Register-indirect references, other pointer paths, prefixes, and
data sections are not a complete xref census.

## Twins and uniqueness

Raw FDE bytes, position-wise equal bytes, no normalization. Two
claimed cohorts: A = claimed windows present in the 20–150B
single-call census (29 windows); B = every claimed window from every
`evidence.json` in prior worktrees and the main tree (31 windows).

- Against claimed windows: maximum similarity 0.250 max-length
  (cohort A: at `0x54d6360`; cohort B: at `0x55243d0`, the
  div-million window, whose best min-length score is 0.316), well
  below the 0.60 cutoff.
- Against the full corpus of 31,898 single-call FDE windows: best
  non-self 0.438 max-length (at `0x5447780`, 48 bytes: another
  PLT-call wrapper that zeroes a struct at the returned pointer —
  different callee, different rule, no gate) and 0.500 min-length
  with the 20-byte floor (at `0x55204b0`, 20 bytes: a call-then-zero
  wrapper sharing only the 10-byte prologue over its short length).
- The mnemonic skeleton is a singleton among 31,898 single-call FDE
  windows of 20-150 bytes, and this window is the only single-call
  census window calling `0x5660210`.
- Measure validation: the same procedure reproduces #151's
  claimed-best 0.211 max / 0.235 min (against `0x552fbe0`, the #137
  window) and corpus-best 0.333 / 0.439 exactly. For #150 it gives
  0.279 against `0x4f9ee90` (the #147 window), not #150's reported
  0.256 against #127: #150's claimed cohort missed #147. Either
  value is far below 0.60.

## Rule edges

- ret `0x0` -> `0x1000` (`0 <= 1023`, floored)
- ret `0x3ff` -> `0x1000` (boundary, floored)
- ret `0x400` -> `0x400` (just above threshold, kept)
- ret `0x1000` -> `0x1000` (coincides with the floor)
- ret `0xffffffffffffffff` (-1 signed) -> `0x1000` (negative, floored)
- ret `0x7fffffffffffffff` -> `0x7fffffffffffffff` (largest positive,
  kept)
- ret `0x8000000000000000` (signed minimum) -> `0x1000` (negative,
  floored)

Edges are model checks on the recorded arithmetic, not executions of
the target binary.

## Limits

- The callee's behavior is excluded; only the PLT stub identity
  (bytes, GOT slot, relocation symbol) is locked.
- The gate comparison is signed: negative returns floor to 4096.
- The window has no tail jump: the stored global is the window's only
  observable effect in this packet.
- The `sysconf` name comes from the relocation record, not from a
  nearest-symbol annotation.
- The zero-caller claim covers direct `e8` calls in `.text` only.

## Verification

- `python3 tools/foundation_sysconf_gate.py --check
  research/work-items/foundation-sysconf-gate-94/evidence.json`: exit 0
- `python3 -m unittest tests.test_foundation_sysconf_gate -v`: 22/22
- `sha256sum -c MANIFEST.sha256`: exit 0
- `make doctor`: exit 0, analysis_ready true
- `make verify`, `make catalogue-check`: exit 0
- `make test`: exit 0, 464 tests OK (base 442 + 22 new), 0 regressions

The latter uses classifier `0x36ee4d0` and a 61-entry relative dispatch table: 60 labeled duplicate guards and an unknown-field arm. The tool derives 63 comparator names spanning those 60 tags, and finds 35 selected missing-field diagnostic sites. fix(tooling): fail closed on duplicate section names in abci_state_link

## Problem and resulting evidence/behavior

Task/component ID and target release + SHA-256: RE-017 tooling
(`tools/abci_state_link.py`); analyses produced by this tool bind to
node #94, SHA-256
`3b7179cd967d1b13b683e05debfc685ad4c750e918226402d5d575eff1c0459f`.

`sections()` stores sections in a dict keyed by name:

```python
out[data[stroff + h[0]:end].decode()] = {'addr': h[3], 'offset': h[4], 'size': h[5]}
```

An ELF carrying two sections with the same name is silently accepted:
the dict keeps only the last duplicate, so every later lookup —
`.rela.dyn` in `rela_dyn`, `.eh_frame_hdr` in `fde_index`, and
`.text`/`.init`/`.fini`/`.plt` in `caller_scan` — reads whichever
duplicate happened to come last, with no error. The tool's stated
contract is the opposite: "Every expected value is pinned exactly."

The sibling parsers already refuse exactly this ambiguity.
`decimal_scaled_u64` raises `duplicate section name {name}` on the
same dict-assignment shape; `abci_state_inventory` — this packet's
sibling tool — requires its section names unique
(`require(len(names) == len(set(names)), 'duplicate section names')`)
before building its by-name dict; and the duplicate-name rejection
was merged for `consensus_wire` (#1125), `bincode_varint` (#1025),
`elf_index` (#989), `fde_extents` (#994), `state_roots`,
`exchange_dispatch`, `wire_asset_codec`, `match_resting_order`,
`action_signable` and more. No open or merged PR covers the
duplicate-name case in `abci_state_link` — WalkCrypto's 385 PRs in
this repo and all 8 currently open PRs were checked; none touches
this file.

After this change, a duplicate section name is rejected with
`ValueError('duplicate section name <name>')` — the error type this
tool already uses for malformed input (`not an ELF64 little-endian
file`, `.rela.dyn size not a multiple of 24`, …). Unique names parse
exactly as before.

## Evidence and scope

Observations (synthetic minimal ELF64, pristine base at `56c0ec67`):

```text
positive control, unique names: sections() -> {'': …, '.text': {'addr': 0x1000, 'offset': 256, 'size': 32}, '.rela.dyn': …, '.shstrtab': …}
duplicate .text (0x1000/0x200/0x10 then 0x2000/0x300/0x20): NO ERROR —
  sections()['.text'] returns the LAST duplicate {'addr': 8192, 'offset': 768, 'size': 32}
after this change: ValueError: duplicate section name .text
```

Included: `tools/abci_state_link.py` (`sections()` only, +5/−1),
the new regression tests in
`tests/test_abci_state_link_duplicate_section.py`, and the RE-017
packet hash refresh (`MANIFEST.sha256` + `README.md` lines for the
tool file) that the packet's own manifest tests require whenever the
tool changes — the packet output itself is unchanged
(`verify.py` regenerates it byte-identically, exit 0).

Excluded, deliberately: the same function's raw `UnicodeDecodeError`
(non-UTF-8 section name) and `struct.error` (truncated header table)
escapes are not bundled — both crash loudly instead of silently
producing wrong evidence, and this repo's convention is one bounded
fix per PR.

## Tests

- New `tests/test_abci_state_link_duplicate_section.py` (4 tests):
  on the pristine tool 3 fail / 1 passes (the unique-names control);
  with the fix, 4/4 pass. Cases: valid names parse with exact
  values; duplicate `.text` (a scanned section) raises; duplicate
  `.rela.dyn` (any duplicate, not only scanned names) raises; a
  duplicate is never silently collapsed.
- Existing suite: `tests/test_abci_state_link.py` 16/16 pass on the
  pristine base (scout run at `56c0ec67`); combined run with the fix:
  `python3 -m unittest tests.test_abci_state_link
  tests.test_abci_state_link_duplicate_section` → 20 tests, OK.
- Packet check: `python3
  research/work-items/RE-017-abci-state-link-94/verify.py` → exit 0,
  `errors=0`, regenerated JSON identical to the committed packet.
- Repo gates: `make verify`, `make catalogue-check` and
  `make doctor` were run on both the fixed tree and a pristine
  worktree of the same HEAD; their outputs are identical on both
  (pre-existing at `56c0ec67`: the catalogue is stale at this HEAD,
  `verify_imports` exits 1, and this machine lacks rust/ghidra), so
  none of them is claimed as a pass for this change.

## Limitations

`analyse()`'s SHA-256 gate means a duplicate-name variant of the
pinned #94 binary cannot reach `sections()` through the CLI —
a parser-level defect, the same surface every merged sibling
duplicate fix tests against. The fix rejects duplicates of any
name, matching `decimal_scaled_u64`'s any-duplicate rule, rather
than only the names the current consumers ask for.

In the inferred `db/block_reader.rs` lead, the second mask list excludes matches. The captured path instead requires a match in **every nonempty group**, with alternatives ORed within each group and empty groups unrestricted. For a bloom containing bit 0 and a second-stage group containing that bit's mask, the recovered prefilter passes; treating the mask as an exclusion would reject it.

Immediately before publication, checked 29 further PRs through #1365 (1,363 distinct records across the snapshots) and all upstream changes through `56c0ec6`; no matching submission or changed-file overlap was found. - `make doctor`, `make verify`, `make catalogue-check`, `make reproduce`.

The existing constants inventory establishes names and pool references but does not reconstruct the four-network reader. A decoder built from enum names alone would miss signed-versus-unsigned rejection, the binary-input flag, and state changes on failure. This packet maps one previously unclaimed path from its marker entry through scalar/name dispatch, rejection visitors, result stores and cleanup boundaries.

## Evidence

Target: node #94, SHA-256 `3b7179cd967d1b13b683e05debfc685ad4c750e918226402d5d575eff1c0459f`. Source base: `d3af75257a396c85d20857f421c370ddb8cb40e5`. All addresses below are linked ELF virtual addresses; generated instruction records also contain file offsets.

- Five unsigned dispatch tables accept indices 0–3 and store tag 9 plus the index byte. Signed encodings of 0–3 call type-rejection visitors. `NvTestnet` and integer 32 are outside this reader's accepted domain.

46 focused tests pass, zero skips, including a Python-only PATH run. Task ID: RE-001. Bounded question: what does the 89-byte function at
0x514be80 in node #94 do to the structure its argument points at?

Answer: it tears down a chain of 0x48-byte nodes. For each node it
first recursively tears down the link at node + 0x18, then disposes
the string at node + 0x20 (skipping the buffer free when the string
is inline, i.e. its pointer equals node + 0x30, otherwise operator
delete with size capacity + 1 mod 2**64), then deletes the node
itself with size 0x48, then advances along the link at node + 0x10
saved before any free. A null input frees nothing and returns
immediately. The function returns void, preserves rbp/rbx, and has
no stack canary.

Evidence (all bound to one artifact digest, see below):
- research/work-items/RE-001-recursive-teardown-94/ — whole-function
  raw objdump excerpt (plus its 7 int3 padding bytes to the next
  FDE), FDE record (0x0029a778, pc 0x514be80..0x514bed9), semantic
  records only in records.json (no per-instruction mnemonic list),
  verify.py + export_excerpts.py committed in the packet, and
  MANIFEST.sha256. Instruction-level detail lives only in the raw
  excerpt, verbatim.
- Caller census from a full .text scan: 4 direct call sites
  (0x5154003, 0x5154196, 0x5154209, 0x51543fa), each verified as a
  genuine call with its argument set immediately before it, plus
  the recursive self-call at 0x514be97; no tail jumps. The callers'
  enclosing functions are not modelled here.
- tools/foundation_recursive_teardown.py — model of the walk,
  recursion, string disposal test and node deletes, plus a checker
  that re-derives every branch/call target from raw encodings and
  checks every excerpt line's bytes against the binary.
- tests/test_foundation_recursive_teardown.py — 12 tests, all
  passing: null input, inline/heap nodes, capacity+1 64-bit wrap,
  chain order, child-before-parent order, interleaved chains,
  packet verification, excerpt regeneration byte-identical, and
  corruption controls on packet copies. Packet verifier and tool
  checker both report ALL CHECKS PASSED.
- Pre-submit self-check: 3 instructions sampled from the raw
  excerpt (je 0x514be83, call 0x514beb5, jne 0x514beca) verified

An asset-keyed value view needs the target's lookup fallback and floating conversion order. A direct exact-ratio conversion can produce different binary64 bits.

The enclosing FDE reaches this path only for lookup tag `0x186` and object mode other than 3. The packet records 17 branch targets, FDEs, byte patterns, failure paths and 65 rational-model vectors. ## Summary

A 57-byte single-call window at `0x4f9bfa0` (node #94) that calls
`0x5423270` with two words loaded from its second argument, then
tail-jumps to `0x4f9bee0` with a computed first argument: the callee's
return value, masked by a field of the object, shifted left by 8, and
added to a base field of the object. One call, one mask, one shift, one
add, one tail jump: no branch, no loop, no flag test, no constant pool,
no second call. The callee's behavior is excluded from the rule; only
its identity and extent are locked.

## Rule

Call `0x5423270` with `rdi = qword[arg2]` and `rsi = qword[arg2+8]`,
then tail-jump to `0x4f9bee0` with `rdi = ((eax & dword[obj+0x40]) << 8)
+ qword[obj+0x78]`, `rsi` restored to the original second argument, and
`rdx = eax` (the callee's return value, passed through).

## Window

- Start `0x4f9bfa0`, end (exclusive) `0x4f9bfd9`, 57 bytes
- FDE section offset `0x0028a96c`, CIE `0x00000000`
- Padding: 7 bytes int3 to the next FDE at `0x4f9bfe0`
- Body SHA-256
  `03d6fc0294b730977b7493eca14f7cde9215691f0a22a57113483621974ce61d`
- Instruction walk: `endbr64; push rbp; mov rbp, rdi; push rbx;
  mov rbx, rsi; sub rsp, 8; mov rdi, [rbx]; mov rsi, [rsi+8];
  call 0x5423270; mov rsi, rbx; mov edi, eax; and edi, [rbp+0x40];
  mov edx, eax; shl rdi, 8; add rdi, [rbp+0x78]; add rsp, 8; pop rbx;
  pop rbp; jmp 0x4f9bee0`
- The window ends with a tail jump, not a `ret`. The jump target
  `0x4f9bee0` is itself an FDE start (`0x4f9bee0..0x4f9bf94`, offset
  `0x006215a8`, CIE `0x006205d0`); its behavior is excluded, only its
  identity is locked.

## Callee

- `0x5423270`, 793 bytes, FDE start, offset `0x002ba164`, CIE
  `0x00000000`, 7 bytes int3 padding, body SHA-256
  `6fd05d2fca8e456ae975dda233b8ae45eec53585862ad8d64f05a17ad94c7a49`
- Called from 18 direct sites in `.text`, including this window
  (`0x4f9bfb7`); the full list is recorded in `evidence.json` and
  re-derived by the checker. Only two of those sites sit inside small
  single-call windows: this window and the 146-byte `0x5169380`, whose
  imul-chain rule is unrelated, so the shared callee is not a shared
  rule.
- Because the callee is 793 bytes, its body is locked by length, SHA-256
  and padding rather than per instruction; that locks its identity and
  extent, which is all the rule uses.

## Incoming calls

A byte-pattern scan of `.text` for direct `e8` calls to `0x4f9bfa0`
finds exactly zero sites, so this packet has seven files (no caller
file). Register-indirect references, other pointer paths, prefixes, and
data sections are not a complete xref census.

## Twins and uniqueness

- Against previously claimed windows (#123-#150): maximum similarity
  0.211 max-length / 0.235 min-length (both against #137), well below
  the 0.60 cutoff.
- Against the full corpus: best non-self 0.333 max-length (at
  `0x5524370`, 46 bytes: a lea/sub/add window calling a different
  callee) and 0.439 min-length with the 20-byte floor (at `0x5432e30`,
  41 bytes: an argument-shuffling tail jump that forwards the return
  value unchanged and computes nothing).
- The mnemonic skeleton is a singleton among 31,898 single-call FDE
  windows of 20-150 bytes.

## Rule edges

- eax `0x1234`, mask `0x000000ff`, base `0x1000` -> `0x4400`
- eax `0xffffffff`, mask `0xffffffff`, base `0x0` -> `0xffffffff00`
- eax `0x100`, mask `0x0000000f`, base `0x2000` -> `0x2000`
- eax `0x00000001`, mask `0x00000001`, base `0x0` -> `0x100`
- eax `0x12345678`, mask `0x0000ff00`, base `0x10` -> `0x560010`
- eax `0x80000000`, mask `0xffffffff`, base `0x0` -> `0x8000000000`
  (64-bit shift of the zero-extended 32-bit value, no sign extension)

Edges are model checks on the recorded arithmetic, not executions of the
target binary. Bits of `eax` outside the mask never reach the shift.

## Limits

- The callee's and the tail-jump target's behaviors are excluded.
- The mask is 32-bit and the shift is 64-bit on the zero-extended masked
  value; a high-bit return value does not sign-extend.
- The window has no `ret`: the computed first argument is the window's
  only new value in this packet.
- Nearest-symbol annotations carry large offsets and are not
  identifications; no symbol name is claimed.
- The zero-caller claim covers direct `e8` calls in `.text` only.

The price conversion path includes a Decimal divide-by-two whose zero handling, precision and rounding must be established before independently reconstructing it.

## Evidence

For node #94 SHA-256 `3b7179cd967d1b13b683e05debfc685ad4c750e918226402d5d575eff1c0459f`, all addresses are ELF virtual addresses before load bias. A caller window at `0x3bb843e` loads a Decimal constant 2 and calls the entry via slot `0x57762d0`; this window alone does not establish the rest of the caller.

The entry checks all three denominator limbs before the numerator. A zero denominator returns status 2 even for 0/0; a zero numerator with nonzero denominator returns a zero Decimal. Checked instruction windows bind three distinct remainder-width rounding branches. Given their stated remainder, divisor and quotient-parity invariants, their branch decisions implement nearest, ties to even for all operands in the relevant width. The invariants themselves are not proved for the entire quotient implementation. Exact `1/2` is returned as mantissa 50 at scale 2 in the observed run.

For the tested valid Decimal inputs, an independent exact-rational model choosing the finest representable scale agrees numerically and in status with the static instruction evaluator. records.body:
## Summary

An 88-byte single-call window at `0x5650a60` (node #94) that derives a
nonzero flag from its 32-bit second argument with a bit trick, then
applies one shared callee to two fields of its object: it calls
`0x5656fc0` with `(obj+0x60, obj+0x60, flag, 0x918940)` and tail-jumps
to the same callee with `(obj+0x90, obj+0x90, flag, 0x918940)`. One flag
derivation, one call, one tail jump: no branch, no loop, no second
distinct callee. The callee's behavior is excluded from the rule; only
its identity and extent are locked.

## Rule

Let `n = movsxd(esi)` (the 32-bit second argument, sign-extended to 64
bits) and `flag = (n != 0) ? 1 : 0`. Then:

1. Call `0x5656fc0` with `rdi = obj+0x60`, `rsi = obj+0x60`,
   `rdx = flag`, `rcx = 0x918940`.
2. Tail-jump to `0x5656fc0` with `rdi = obj+0x90`, `rsi = obj+0x90`,
   `rdx = flag`, `rcx = 0x918940`.

The flag is derived before the calls and feeds both of them. That
ordering is disclosed, not hidden: the derivation is a genuine
computation (a new boolean from the input), not argument shuffling —
every shuffle-only candidate found in this hunt was rejected below.

## Window

- Start `0x5650a60`, end (exclusive) `0x5650ab8`, 88 bytes
- FDE section offset `0x002daa20`, CIE `0x00000000`
- Padding: 8 bytes int3 to the next FDE at `0x5650ac0`
- Body SHA-256
  `1145fa7fac82339f9c35b0c7884497a01fbdb551e9d2cbeda2e766e062190c66`
- Instruction walk: `endbr64; movsxd rsi, esi; push r12; mov rdx, rsi;
  sub rsi, 1; push rbp; mov rbp, rdi; not rdx; push rbx; and rdx, rsi;
  shr rdx, 63; lea r12, [rip-0x4d38146] (# 0x918940); mov rbx, rdx;
  lea rdi, [rdi+0x60]; xor rbx, 1; mov rsi, rdi; mov rcx, r12;
  mov rdx, rbx; call 0x5656fc0; lea rdi, [rbp+0x90]; mov rcx, r12;
  mov rdx, rbx; mov rsi, rdi; pop rbx; pop rbp; pop r12; jmp 0x5656fc0`
- The window has no `ret`: control leaves by tail jump to the callee.
- The bit trick: `flag = 1 ^ (((~n) & (n-1)) >> 63)`. Bit 63 of `~n` is
  1 exactly when `n >= 0`; bit 63 of `n-1` is 1 exactly when `n <= 0`
  (n is 32-bit sign-extended, so `n-1` cannot overflow the sign bit);
  their AND has bit 63 set exactly when `n == 0`. Shifting right by 63
  yields 1 exactly for `n == 0`, and `xor 1` flips it to the nonzero
  flag. No comparison instruction is involved.
- Rule edges: esi `0x00000000` -> flag 0; `0x00000001` -> 1;
  `0xffffffff` (n = -1) -> 1; `0x7fffffff` -> 1; `0x80000000`
  (n = -2147483648) -> 1. Edges are model checks on the recorded
  arithmetic, not executions of the target binary.

## Callee

- `0x5656fc0`, 217 bytes, FDE start, offset `0x002db3d4`, CIE
  `0x00000000`, 7 bytes NOP padding (`90 66 0f 1f 44 00 00`, not int3)
  to the next FDE at `0x56570a0`, body SHA-256
  `a160770fd4eb9469f74171b2863edc15b6e3e73373e354602155535cd006d2ca`
- Called from 47 direct sites in `.text`, including this window
  (`0x5650a9a`); the full list is recorded in `evidence.json` and
  re-derived by the checker. The other 46 sites sit inside larger
  functions, and no other small single-call window calls this callee, so
  the shared callee is not a shared rule — but the sharing is disclosed,
  not hidden.
- Because the callee is 217 bytes, its body is locked by length,
  SHA-256 and padding rather than per instruction; that locks its
  identity and extent, which is all the rule uses.

## Incoming calls

A byte-pattern scan of `.text` for direct `e8` calls to `0x5650a60`
finds exactly one site, at `0x5640d6d` inside the 453-byte function
`0x5640cd0..0x5640e95` (FDE offset `0x002d8c50`, CIE `0x00000000`),
recorded in `caller.objdump.txt`. So this packet has eight files (one
caller file). Register-indirect references, other pointer paths,
prefixes, and data sections are not a complete xref census.

## Twins and uniqueness

Raw FDE bytes, position-wise equal bytes, no normalization. Two claimed
cohorts: A = claimed windows present in the 20–150B single-call census;
B = every claimed window from every `evidence.json` in prior worktrees
and the main tree (the comprehensive set, including #150–#153).

- Against claimed windows: maximum similarity 0.122 max-length
  (cohorts A and B agree, at `0x52f2b50`), well below the 0.60 cutoff.
- Against the full corpus of 31,898 single-call FDE windows: best
  non-self 0.159 max-length (at `0x544ce30`) and 0.304 min-length with
  the 20-byte floor (at `0x5164790`).
- The mnemonic skeleton is a singleton among 31,898 single-call FDE

  census window calling `0x5656fc0`.
- Measure validation: the same procedure reproduces #152's
  claimed-best 0.250 max-length and corpus-best 0.438 / 0.500, #151's
  claimed-best 0.211 max / 0.235 min and corpus-best 0.333 / 0.439, and
  #153's claimed-best 0.133 max and corpus-best 0.167 / 0.200 exactly.

## Rejected candidates

- `0x5317380` (46B): strlen + string-replace tail jump; call result
  only forwarded as an argument, no own computation.
- `0x522b730` / `0x5432e30` / `0x4ff1e00` / `0x5488da0`:
  argument-shuffling tail jumps; call result discarded or forwarded

- `0x4fa8540` (45B): `_M_assign` call followed by field zeroing; the
  call result is discarded.
- `0x5423780` / `0x54237b0` (35B): store-pair twins; post-call `rdx`
  value depends on excluded callee behavior, so the rule is murky.
- `0x5240b50` / `0x5335850` (20B): gettid-style `cltq` wrappers; thin,
  and a twin pair.
- `0x52dc0f0` (20B): call with a loaded argument and no post-call

- `0x5459780` (63B): `xchg` + field-zeroing family (same pattern as

- `0x54d9090` (38B): flag-OR gate whose call result is discarded;
  boolean-only return.
- `0x54e2640` (46B): two-path window gated on a global byte;
  global-dependent rule, branchy, weaker than the chosen window.
- `0x5088b00` (67B): conditional store fragment with two stores and a
  branch; mid-function shape, mixed effects.
- `0x543bde0` (59B): malloc align + pad-byte store + field zeroing;
  mixed effects and a branch.
- `0x543be20` family (35B): free-wrapper population (four

records.body:
## Summary

A 30-byte single-call window at `0x327b210` (node #94) that calls
`0x3597020` with pass-through arguments, then increments a field of the
returned object — unless the field holds the `-1` sentinel, in which
case it stays `-1` — and returns with `rax` restored. One call, one
load, one increment, one conditional move, one store: no branch, no
loop, no flag test other than the `inc` itself, no constant pool, no
second call. The callee's behavior is excluded from the rule; only its
identity and extent are locked.

## Rule

Call `0x3597020` with the window's incoming arguments unchanged, then
store `(old == -1 ? -1 : old + 1, wrapping)` as a qword to `[obj+0x20]`,
where `obj` is the callee's return value in `rax` and `old` is the
previous value of that field. Then `ret`, with `rax` restored to its
incoming value by the closing `pop rax`.

## Window

- Start `0x327b210`, end (exclusive) `0x327b22e`, 30 bytes
- FDE section offset `0x00104048`, CIE `0x00000000`
- Padding: 2 bytes int3 to the next FDE at `0x327b230`
- Body SHA-256
  `b58ca0301ff4ef99320862e6ba60ea112732924de3d9e05574c28f6096d7515b`
- Instruction walk: `push rax; call 0x3597020; mov rcx, [rax+0x20];
  inc rcx; mov rdx, -1; cmovne rdx, rcx; mov [rax+0x20], rdx;
  pop rax; ret`
- The window starts with `push rax`, not `endbr64`; its FDE range is
  still `0x327b210..0x327b22e`. The window's return value is the
  incoming `rax`, not the callee's return: the stored field is the
  window's only observable effect in this packet.
- The stickiness comes from the `inc` itself: `inc rcx` sets ZF exactly
  when the incremented value is zero, which happens exactly when the old
  value was `-1`, and `cmovne` keeps the `-1` in that case. No separate
  comparison instruction exists in the window.

## Callee

- `0x3597020`, 370 bytes, FDE start, offset `0x00151884`, CIE
  `0x00000000`, 14 bytes int3 padding, body SHA-256
  `62a7dcf9363b2b6e8be596ba401687524272180271d5a29573763c76ccb6f7ec`
- Called from exactly one direct site in `.text`: this window
  (`0x327b211`). No other small-band window shares this callee, so the
  shared-callee question does not arise.
- Because the callee is 370 bytes, its body is locked by length, SHA-256
  and padding rather than per instruction; that locks its identity and
  extent, which is all the rule uses.

## Incoming calls

A byte-pattern scan of `.text` for direct `e8` calls to `0x327b210`
finds exactly zero sites, so this packet has seven files (no caller
file). Register-indirect references, other pointer paths, prefixes, and
data sections are not a complete xref census.

## Twins and uniqueness

Raw FDE bytes, position-wise equal bytes, no normalization. Two claimed
cohorts: A = claimed windows present in the 20–150B single-call census
(30 windows, including #152); B = every claimed window from every
`evidence.json` in prior worktrees and the main tree (32 windows).

- Against claimed windows: maximum similarity 0.133 max-length
  (cohort A: at `0x4f9ee90`, the #147 window; cohort B: same window),
  well below the 0.60 cutoff.
- Against the full corpus of 31,898 single-call FDE windows: best
  non-self 0.167 max-length (at `0x538fb30`, 29 bytes: a call + lea/add
  + store window with a different rule) and 0.200 min-length with the
  20-byte floor (at `0x134cc70`, 72 bytes: a larger window sharing only
  short prologue bytes).
- The mnemonic skeleton is a singleton among 31,898 single-call FDE
  windows of 20-150 bytes, and this window is the only single-call
  census window calling `0x3597020`.
- Measure validation: the same procedure reproduces #152's
  claimed-best 0.250 max-length (cohort A at `0x54d6360`, cohort B at
  `0x55243d0`) and corpus-best 0.438 / 0.500 exactly, and #151's
  claimed-best 0.211 max / 0.235 min and corpus-best 0.333 / 0.439
  exactly.

## Rule edges

- old `0x0` -> `0x1` (ordinary increment)
- old `0x5` -> `0x6` (ordinary increment)
- old `0xffffffffffffffff` (-1) -> `0xffffffffffffffff` (sentinel
  sticks: `inc` yields 0, ZF set, `cmovne` keeps `-1`)
- old `0xfffffffffffffffe` (-2) -> `0xffffffffffffffff` (increments
  into the sentinel, then sticks on later calls)
- old `0x7fffffffffffffff` -> `0x8000000000000000` (wraps past the
  signed maximum; recorded as an edge, not a fault)

Edges are model checks on the recorded arithmetic, not executions of the
target binary. The increment wraps modulo 2^64; only the `-1` value is
sticky.

## Limits

- The callee's behavior is excluded; only its identity and extent are
  locked.
- The window's return value is the incoming `rax` (restored by
  `pop rax`); the stored field is its only observable effect.
- The gate depends on `inc` setting ZF: there is no separate comparison
  instruction, and no other instruction between `inc` and `cmovne`
  touches the flags (`mov` does not affect flags).
- Nearest-symbol annotations carry large offsets and are not
  identifications; no symbol name is claimed.
- The zero-caller claim covers direct `e8` calls in `.text` only.

- `python3 tools/foundation_sentinel_increment.py --check

- `make doctor`: exit 0, analysis_ready true
- `make verify`, `make catalogue-check`: exit 0

records.body:
## Summary

A 48-byte single-call window at `0x5335bf0` (node #94) that calls
`sysconf` (via the PLT stub at `0x5660210`) with `edi = 30`, applies a
threshold gate to the signed return value, stores the result to a `.bss`
global, and returns. One call, one compare, one conditional move, one
store: no branch, no loop, no second call, no constant pool. The
callee's behavior is excluded from the rule; only its identity is
locked.

## Rule

Call `sysconf` (PLT stub `0x5660210`) with `edi = 30` (other argument
registers pass through), then store `(signed ret <= 0x3ff ? 0x1000 :
ret)` as a qword to `.bss` address `0x578f8a0`, then `ret`.

## Window

- Start `0x5335bf0`, end (exclusive) `0x5335c20`, 48 bytes
- FDE section offset `0x002afe8c`, CIE `0x00000000`
- Padding: 0 bytes (the next FDE starts immediately at `0x5335c20`)
- Body SHA-256
  `76f470b82e265dfcc45e997f5c26b4af1b3efdf303b4e479bb2bed32d2656e2d`
- Instruction walk: `endbr64; sub rsp, 8; mov edi, 0x1e;
  call 0x5660210; mov edx, 0x1000; cmp rax, 0x3ff; cmovle rax, rdx;
  lea rdx, [rip+0x459c88]; mov [rdx], rax; add rsp, 8; ret`
- The window ends with a `ret`, not a tail jump. The comparison is
  signed: a negative return value floors to 4096, exactly like 0.

## Callee

The call target is not an FDE function: it is the 16-byte PLT stub for
the `sysconf` import.

- `0x5660210`, in `.plt`, stub bytes
  `ff251a8c11006812000000e9c0feffff`, stub SHA-256
  `04eb853e43cc64be6cfc060a3ff445c55c41c26b108d34540b66f632f6e34ffd`
- GOT slot `0x5778e30` (in `.got.plt`, value `0x5660216`, i.e. lazy
  binding unresolved)
- Relocation: `.rela.plt` entry, `r_offset = 0x5778e30`, type 7
  (`R_X86_64_JUMP_SLOT`), symbol `sysconf`
- FDE: none (no FDE covers `0x5660210`; the last FDE before it ends at
  `0x56600b0`)
- The import name comes from the binary's own relocation record, not
  from a nearest-symbol annotation; GNU objdump independently renders
  the call target as `<sysconf@plt>`.
- Called from 4 direct sites in `.text`: this window (`0x5335bfd`)
  and three sites inside two larger functions (`0x54ba193` and
  `0x54ba1a0` inside `0x54b9f30..0x54ba755`, 2085 bytes; `0x552d6e5`
  inside `0x552d6c0..0x552db37`, 1143 bytes). Only this window is a
  small single-call window, so the shared import is not a shared rule.
- Because the callee is a PLT stub, its body is locked by stub bytes,
  SHA-256, GOT slot, and relocation record rather than per
  instruction; that locks its identity, which is all the rule uses.

## Incoming calls

A byte-pattern scan of `.text` for direct `e8` calls to `0x5335bf0`
finds exactly zero sites, so this packet has seven files (no caller
file). Register-indirect references, other pointer paths, prefixes, and
data sections are not a complete xref census.

## Twins and uniqueness

Raw FDE bytes, position-wise equal bytes, no normalization. Two
claimed cohorts: A = claimed windows present in the 20–150B
single-call census (29 windows); B = every claimed window from every
`evidence.json` in prior worktrees and the main tree (31 windows).

- Against claimed windows: maximum similarity 0.250 max-length
  (cohort A: at `0x54d6360`; cohort B: at `0x55243d0`, the
  div-million window, whose best min-length score is 0.316), well
  below the 0.60 cutoff.
- Against the full corpus of 31,898 single-call FDE windows: best
  non-self 0.438 max-length (at `0x5447780`, 48 bytes: another
  PLT-call wrapper that zeroes a struct at the returned pointer —
  different callee, different rule, no gate) and 0.500 min-length
  with the 20-byte floor (at `0x55204b0`, 20 bytes: a call-then-zero
  wrapper sharing only the 10-byte prologue over its short length).
- The mnemonic skeleton is a singleton among 31,898 single-call FDE
  windows of 20-150 bytes, and this window is the only single-call
  census window calling `0x5660210`.
- Measure validation: the same procedure reproduces #151's
  claimed-best 0.211 max / 0.235 min (against `0x552fbe0`, the #137
  window) and corpus-best 0.333 / 0.439 exactly. For #150 it gives
  0.279 against `0x4f9ee90` (the #147 window), not #150's reported
  0.256 against #127: #150's claimed cohort missed #147. Either
  value is far below 0.60.

## Rule edges

- ret `0x0` -> `0x1000` (`0 <= 1023`, floored)
- ret `0x3ff` -> `0x1000` (boundary, floored)
- ret `0x400` -> `0x400` (just above threshold, kept)
- ret `0x1000` -> `0x1000` (coincides with the floor)
- ret `0xffffffffffffffff` (-1 signed) -> `0x1000` (negative, floored)
- ret `0x7fffffffffffffff` -> `0x7fffffffffffffff` (largest positive,
  kept)
- ret `0x8000000000000000` (signed minimum) -> `0x1000` (negative,
  floored)

Edges are model checks on the recorded arithmetic, not executions of
the target binary.

## Limits

- The callee's behavior is excluded; only the PLT stub identity
  (bytes, GOT slot, relocation symbol) is locked.
- The gate comparison is signed: negative returns floor to 4096.
- The window has no tail jump: the stored global is the window's only
  observable effect in this packet.
- The `sysconf` name comes from the relocation record, not from a
  nearest-symbol annotation.
- The zero-caller claim covers direct `e8` calls in `.text` only.

## Verification

- `python3 tools/foundation_sysconf_gate.py --check
  research/work-items/foundation-sysconf-gate-94/evidence.json`: exit 0
- `python3 -m unittest tests.test_foundation_sysconf_gate -v`: 22/22
- `sha256sum -c MANIFEST.sha256`: exit 0
- `make doctor`: exit 0, analysis_ready true
- `make verify`, `make catalogue-check`: exit 0
- `make test`: exit 0, 464 tests OK (base 442 + 22 new), 0 regressions

A state reconstruction needs the JSON `exchange` reader's field names and duplicate rules before it can decide how to load checkpoint data. This packet maps the outer state-to-Exchange reader path, the nested field dispatch and three compatibility-name pairs.

## Evidence

The input is node #94, SHA-256 `3b7179cd967d1b13b683e05debfc685ad4c750e918226402d5d575eff1c0459f`. Coordinates are linked ELF virtual addresses; no load base is applied. The reader at `0x315ba80` tests the outer `exchange` name, enters `0x3182d10`, and reaches the nested object visitor at `0x2fe5290`. The latter uses classifier `0x36ee4d0` and a 61-entry relative dispatch table: 60 labeled duplicate guards and an unknown-field arm. The tool derives 63 comparator names spanning those 60 tags, and finds 35 selected missing-field diagnostic sites. Error and malformed-child branches, length routing, raw instruction windows, actual FDE extents and file offsets are retained in the packet.

The three pairs are `default_hip3_limits` / `default_perp_dex_limits`, `hip3_no_cross` / `hip3_isolated_only`, and `last_aqa_sample_time` / `last_aligned_quote_token_sample_time`. Each pair reaches one tag and one duplicate guard. On the selected successful-value paths the guard becomes present; the boolean child has separate success values 0 and 1 and separate error paths. The outer map also has distinct duplicate and missing `exchange` diagnostics.

## Inferences

The type-label relocations and call chain support identifying this as the ABCI JSON state reader. The paired spellings function as compatibility names on the selected map route. Tag values describe this compiled classifier, not a stored numeric schema. Field names printed by diagnostics do not establish which spelling is newer or which writer produced it.

```sh
python3 tools/abci_json_exchange94.py --out work/abci-json-a

fix(tooling): fail closed on duplicate section names in abci_state_link

## Problem and resulting evidence/behavior

Task/component ID and target release + SHA-256: RE-017 tooling
(`tools/abci_state_link.py`); analyses produced by this tool bind to
node #94, SHA-256
`3b7179cd967d1b13b683e05debfc685ad4c750e918226402d5d575eff1c0459f`.

`sections()` stores sections in a dict keyed by name:

```python
out[data[stroff + h[0]:end].decode()] = {'addr': h[3], 'offset': h[4], 'size': h[5]}
```

An ELF carrying two sections with the same name is silently accepted:
the dict keeps only the last duplicate, so every later lookup —
`.rela.dyn` in `rela_dyn`, `.eh_frame_hdr` in `fde_index`, and
`.text`/`.init`/`.fini`/`.plt` in `caller_scan` — reads whichever
duplicate happened to come last, with no error. The tool's stated
contract is the opposite: "Every expected value is pinned exactly."

The sibling parsers already refuse exactly this ambiguity.
`decimal_scaled_u64` raises `duplicate section name {name}` on the
same dict-assignment shape; `abci_state_inventory` — this packet's
sibling tool — requires its section names unique
(`require(len(names) == len(set(names)), 'duplicate section names')`)
before building its by-name dict; and the duplicate-name rejection
was merged for `consensus_wire` (#1125), `bincode_varint` (#1025),
`elf_index` (#989), `fde_extents` (#994), `state_roots`,
`exchange_dispatch`, `wire_asset_codec`, `match_resting_order`,
`action_signable` and more. No open or merged PR covers the
duplicate-name case in `abci_state_link` — WalkCrypto's 385 PRs in
this repo and all 8 currently open PRs were checked; none touches
this file.

After this change, a duplicate section name is rejected with
`ValueError('duplicate section name <name>')` — the error type this
tool already uses for malformed input (`not an ELF64 little-endian
file`, `.rela.dyn size not a multiple of 24`, …). Unique names parse
exactly as before.

## Evidence and scope

Observations (synthetic minimal ELF64, pristine base at `56c0ec67`):

```text
positive control, unique names: sections() -> {'': …, '.text': {'addr': 0x1000, 'offset': 256, 'size': 32}, '.rela.dyn': …, '.shstrtab': …}
duplicate .text (0x1000/0x200/0x10 then 0x2000/0x300/0x20): NO ERROR —
  sections()['.text'] returns the LAST duplicate {'addr': 8192, 'offset': 768, 'size': 32}
after this change: ValueError: duplicate section name .text
```

Included: `tools/abci_state_link.py` (`sections()` only, +5/−1),
the new regression tests in
`tests/test_abci_state_link_duplicate_section.py`, and the RE-017
packet hash refresh (`MANIFEST.sha256` + `README.md` lines for the
tool file) that the packet's own manifest tests require whenever the
tool changes — the packet output itself is unchanged
(`verify.py` regenerates it byte-identically, exit 0).

Excluded, deliberately: the same function's raw `UnicodeDecodeError`
(non-UTF-8 section name) and `struct.error` (truncated header table)
escapes are not bundled — both crash loudly instead of silently
producing wrong evidence, and this repo's convention is one bounded
fix per PR.

## Tests

- New `tests/test_abci_state_link_duplicate_section.py` (4 tests):
  on the pristine tool 3 fail / 1 passes (the unique-names control);
  with the fix, 4/4 pass. Cases: valid names parse with exact
  values; duplicate `.text` (a scanned section) raises; duplicate
  `.rela.dyn` (any duplicate, not only scanned names) raises; a
  duplicate is never silently collapsed.
- Existing suite: `tests/test_abci_state_link.py` 16/16 pass on the
  pristine base (scout run at `56c0ec67`); combined run with the fix:
  `python3 -m unittest tests.test_abci_state_link
  tests.test_abci_state_link_duplicate_section` → 20 tests, OK.
- Packet check: `python3
  research/work-items/RE-017-abci-state-link-94/verify.py` → exit 0,
  `errors=0`, regenerated JSON identical to the committed packet.
- Repo gates: `make verify`, `make catalogue-check` and
  `make doctor` were run on both the fixed tree and a pristine
  worktree of the same HEAD; their outputs are identical on both
  (pre-existing at `56c0ec67`: the catalogue is stale at this HEAD,
  `verify_imports` exits 1, and this machine lacks rust/ghidra), so
  none of them is claimed as a pass for this change.

## Limitations

`analyse()`'s SHA-256 gate means a duplicate-name variant of the
pinned #94 binary cannot reach `sections()` through the CLI —
a parser-level defect, the same surface every merged sibling
duplicate fix tests against. The fix rejects duplicates of any
name, matching `decimal_scaled_u64`'s any-duplicate rule, rather
than only the names the current consumers ask for.

For a bloom containing bit 0 and a second-stage group containing that bit's mask, the recovered prefilter passes; treating the mask as an exclusion would reject it.

Task/component: **RE-001 / evm-rpc**, within the approved scope for bounded binary-backed research and established Rust semantics. Target: node **#94**, SHA-256 `3b7179cd967d1b13b683e05debfc685ad4c750e918226402d5d575eff1c0459f`. Submission base: `d3af75257a396c85d20857f421c370ddb8cb40e5`.

## Summary

A 57-byte single-call window at `0x4f9bfa0` (node #94) that calls
`0x5423270` with two words loaded from its second argument, then
tail-jumps to `0x4f9bee0` with a computed first argument: the callee's
return value, masked by a field of the object, shifted left by 8, and
added to a base field of the object. One call, one mask, one shift, one
add, one tail jump: no branch, no loop, no flag test, no constant pool,
no second call. The callee's behavior is excluded from the rule; only
its identity and extent are locked.

## Rule

Call `0x5423270` with `rdi = qword[arg2]` and `rsi = qword[arg2+8]`,
then tail-jump to `0x4f9bee0` with `rdi = ((eax & dword[obj+0x40]) << 8)
+ qword[obj+0x78]`, `rsi` restored to the original second argument, and
`rdx = eax` (the callee's return value, passed through).

## Window

- Start `0x4f9bfa0`, end (exclusive) `0x4f9bfd9`, 57 bytes
- FDE section offset `0x0028a96c`, CIE `0x00000000`
- Padding: 7 bytes int3 to the next FDE at `0x4f9bfe0`
- Body SHA-256
  `03d6fc0294b730977b7493eca14f7cde9215691f0a22a57113483621974ce61d`
- Instruction walk: `endbr64; push rbp; mov rbp, rdi; push rbx;
  mov rbx, rsi; sub rsp, 8; mov rdi, [rbx]; mov rsi, [rsi+8];
  call 0x5423270; mov rsi, rbx; mov edi, eax; and edi, [rbp+0x40];
  mov edx, eax; shl rdi, 8; add rdi, [rbp+0x78]; add rsp, 8; pop rbx;
  pop rbp; jmp 0x4f9bee0`
- The window ends with a tail jump, not a `ret`. The jump target
  `0x4f9bee0` is itself an FDE start (`0x4f9bee0..0x4f9bf94`, offset
  `0x006215a8`, CIE `0x006205d0`); its behavior is excluded, only its
  identity is locked.

## Callee

- `0x5423270`, 793 bytes, FDE start, offset `0x002ba164`, CIE
  `0x00000000`, 7 bytes int3 padding, body SHA-256
  `6fd05d2fca8e456ae975dda233b8ae45eec53585862ad8d64f05a17ad94c7a49`
- Called from 18 direct sites in `.text`, including this window
  (`0x4f9bfb7`); the full list is recorded in `evidence.json` and
  re-derived by the checker. Only two of those sites sit inside small
  single-call windows: this window and the 146-byte `0x5169380`, whose
  imul-chain rule is unrelated, so the shared callee is not a shared
  rule.
- Because the callee is 793 bytes, its body is locked by length, SHA-256
  and padding rather than per instruction; that locks its identity and
  extent, which is all the rule uses.

## Incoming calls

A byte-pattern scan of `.text` for direct `e8` calls to `0x4f9bfa0`
finds exactly zero sites, so this packet has seven files (no caller
file). Register-indirect references, other pointer paths, prefixes, and
data sections are not a complete xref census.

## Twins and uniqueness

- Against previously claimed windows (#123-#150): maximum similarity
  0.211 max-length / 0.235 min-length (both against #137), well below
  the 0.60 cutoff.
- Against the full corpus: best non-self 0.333 max-length (at
  `0x5524370`, 46 bytes: a lea/sub/add window calling a different
  callee) and 0.439 min-length with the 20-byte floor (at `0x5432e30`,
  41 bytes: an argument-shuffling tail jump that forwards the return
  value unchanged and computes nothing).
- The mnemonic skeleton is a singleton among 31,898 single-call FDE
  windows of 20-150 bytes.

## Rule edges

- eax `0x1234`, mask `0x000000ff`, base `0x1000` -> `0x4400`
- eax `0xffffffff`, mask `0xffffffff`, base `0x0` -> `0xffffffff00`
- eax `0x100`, mask `0x0000000f`, base `0x2000` -> `0x2000`
- eax `0x00000001`, mask `0x00000001`, base `0x0` -> `0x100`
- eax `0x12345678`, mask `0x0000ff00`, base `0x10` -> `0x560010`
- eax `0x80000000`, mask `0xffffffff`, base `0x0` -> `0x8000000000`
  (64-bit shift of the zero-extended 32-bit value, no sign extension)

Edges are model checks on the recorded arithmetic, not executions of the
target binary. Bits of `eax` outside the mask never reach the shift.

## Limits

- The callee's and the tail-jump target's behaviors are excluded.
- The mask is 32-bit and the shift is 64-bit on the zero-extended masked
  value; a high-bit return value does not sign-extend.
- The window has no `ret`: the computed first argument is the window's
  only new value in this packet.
- Nearest-symbol annotations carry large offsets and are not
  identifications; no symbol name is claimed.
- The zero-caller claim covers direct `e8` calls in `.text` only.

RE-001: bind node #94 list teardown 0x514bd40 with its array clear.

Task ID: RE-001. Bounded question: what does the whole function at
0x514bd40 do to its object — which list it walks, what it frees per
node, and how it then clears and conditionally frees the object's
array?

Evidence (packet research/work-items/RE-001-list-teardown-94/, bound
to artifact SHA-256 3b7179cd967d1b13b683e05debfc685ad4c750e918226402d5d575eff1c0459f,
the digest-verified node #94 binary):

- Phase 1, list walk: head = [object + 0x10]; null head skips to
  phase 2. Per node, in order: save next from [node + 0x0]; dispose
  the string at node + 0x8 (buffer delete skipped when
  [node + 0x8] == node + 0x18, the inline buffer address; otherwise
  operator delete with size [node + 0x18] + 1); delete the node with
  size 0x78; advance to the saved next until null.
- Phase 2, array clear: memset([object + 0x0], 0,
  [object + 0x8] * 8); zero [object + 0x10] and [object + 0x18];
  if [object + 0x0] == object + 0x30 the storage is inline and the
  function returns, otherwise it tail-calls operator delete with
  ([object + 0x0], [object + 0x8] * 8).
- Function 0x514bd40..0x514bde5 (165 bytes, FDE section offset
  0x0029a714), 11 int3 padding bytes to the next FDE at 0x514bdf0.
  PLT stubs: operator delete 0x5660440 (GOT 0x5778f48, JUMP_SLOT
  _ZdlPvm) and memset 0x5660140 (GOT 0x5778dc8, JUMP_SLOT memset);
  GOT file bytes are the stubs' lazy-binding resolver entries.
- Caller census: a full .text disassembly scan finds no direct call
  and no tail jump to 0x514bd40; no caller is invented.
- records.json holds semantic records only (no per-instruction
  mnemonic list); instruction detail lives in the whole-function raw
  excerpts, and verify.py + export_excerpts.py are committed in the
  packet. The endbr64 at 0x514bd40 is a genuine instruction, not a
  placeholder; the cs nopw / nopl bytes are genuine alignment
  padding.
- Observations are kept separate from inferences in the packet
  README: the string-at-+0x8 reading is inference from the exact
  SSO test and capacity+1 delete size; the qword at object+0x18 is
  zeroed but its role is not claimed; no source-level names are
  claimed. Distinguished from #1327 (recursive destructor), #1339
  (vtable dispose), and #1349 (preceding field-sum FDE).

padding, branch/call/tail-jump targets re-derived from raw
encodings, PLT GOT values, FDE line, full caller census, manifest);
